description: Concurrent use substantially increases risk of severe gastrointestinal and intracranial bleeding due to combined antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects.
Iodinated radiocontrast can precipitate acute renal impairment leading to fatal metformin accumulation and lactic acidosis.
NSAIDs attenuate the antihypertensive efficacy of angiotensin receptor blockers and increase risk of acute renal failure.
Concomitant use may result in severe hyperkalemia, particularly in patients with pre-existing renal impairment.
Penicillins decrease renal clearance of methotrexate leading to severe bone marrow toxicity and pancytopenia.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors markedly increase atorvastatin plasma concentrations, elevating risk of rhabdomyolysis and myopathy.
Chronic or acute ethanol ingestion potentiates the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism, elevating risk of lactic acidosis.
Proton pump inhibitors may modestly decrease hepatic bioactivation of clopidogrel via CYP2C19, reducing antiplatelet efficacy.
Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 metabolism of theophylline, leading to toxic plasma levels, seizures, and arrhythmias.
Regular prolonged paracetamol use (>2g/day) enhances anticoagulant effect of warfarin, prolonging INR and increasing bleeding risk.
Amlodipine increases systemic exposure of simvastatin. Limit simvastatin dose to 20mg daily to prevent myopathy.
Combination significantly increases risk of severe life-threatening hyperkalemia. Close serum potassium monitoring required.
Calcium salts bind levothyroxine in the gastrointestinal tract, significantly reducing thyroid hormone absorption.
Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein efflux of digoxin, doubling serum digoxin concentrations and causing fatal cardiotoxicity.
Combined serotonergic agents increase risk of Serotonin Syndrome and lower seizure threshold.
Concomitant administration significantly prolongs QTc interval, precipitating Torsades de Pointes and ventricular arrhythmias.
Additive ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity between loop diuretics and aminoglycosides. Avoid concurrent administration.
Gastric acid suppression reduces ionization and absorption of dietary and supplemental non-heme iron salts.
Concomitant NSAID and systemic corticosteroid therapy causes synergistically elevated risk of gastrointestinal ulceration and perforation.
Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 metabolism of sulfonylureas, causing severe prolonged hypoglycemia.
NSAIDs decrease renal prostaglandin synthesis, impairing lithium excretion and precipitating acute lithium toxicity.
Protein displacement and metabolic interaction leading to increased free phenytoin levels and hepatotoxicity.
Profound negative inotropic and dromotropic effects leading to severe bradycardia, heart block, and cardiogenic shock.
Macrolides inhibit carbamazepine clearance, resulting in acute ataxia, vertigo, nystagmus, and toxic encephalopathy.
Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase conversion of 6-mercaptopurine, leading to fatal bone marrow suppression.
